CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING AGENDA
April 6, 2022 7:00 P.M.
City Council Chambers – Ninth Floor (Planning Commission & Staff)
1 West Manchester Boulevard

  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS
Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social
distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to Assembly
Bill 361, please note that members of the public will only be allowed
to observe and address the Planning Commission of April 6, 2022 at
7:00 P.M. by telephone, video and other means, as follows:

Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members
of the public may listen and make oral public comments
telephonically by dialing:

  Phone Number: 888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694
  Access Code: 9541871#

Please observe the following tips when phoning in:
   When you call-in, the operator will provide further
  instructions on how you can make public comments via phone.
   If you are calling from a cell phone, please call from an area
  with good reception.
   If you are watching the meeting on Facebook or Channel 35 while
  also accessing the phone line, it is requested that you mute the
  sound of your video feed as it is offset by 3 seconds from the
  phone transmission. Additionally, when you are making public
  comments on the phone line you will be inaudible due to feedback.

Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:
   On Spectrum Cable Local Channel 35 with audio and limited video.
  Please check with your cable provider for details.
   Live on-line through Facebook Live, with audio and limited
  video, at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

Written Public Comments: Members of the public can submit comments
for consideration by the Planning Commission by sending them to
Bernard  McCrumby,  Acting  Planning  Manager  at
bmccrumby@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members
of the Planning Commission prior to consideration of the agenda,
comments must be received prior to 12:00 P.M. on the day of the
meeting. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda
item. Comments received after 12:00 P.M. and prior to close of the
public hearing will be made part of the official public record of the
meeting.

Accessibility: If you will require special accommodations due to a
disability, please contact the Planning Division Office at (310) 412-
5230, One Manchester Boulevard, 4th Floor, Inglewood, California
90301.  All requests for accommodations must be received 48 hours
prior to the day of the hearing.

Spanish: "Si no entiende esta noticia o si necesita  más
información, favor de llamar a este número (310) 412-5230."

Pages]
 1.  Pledge of Allegiance.

2.  Roll Call.

3.  Communications from staff.

4.  Public Comments Regarding Agenda Items. Persons wishing to
  address the Planning Commission on any item on the agenda
  other than a public hearing may do so at this time.

5.  Minutes approval  for  March  2,  2022  Planning  Commission
  meetings.

6.  NON-PUBLIC HEARING
  a. A non-public hearing to consider new rooftop solar panels
  on an existing, 4-story medical office building parking
  structure on an H-C (Historic Core) zoned property at 110
  North La Brea Avenue
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2022-026; and
  2) Adopt the attached resolution approving DR-2022-
  005 subject to 8 conditions, and/or add conditions
  as deemed appropriate.
  Item 6a documents

  b. A non-public hearing to consider exterior alterations to
  an existing two-story commercial building on an H-C
  (Historic Core) zoned property at 132 North Market Street.
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2022-032; and
  2) Adopt the attached resolution approving DR-2022-
  006 subject to 9 conditions, and/or add conditions
  as deemed appropriate.
  Item 6b documents

7.  Public Comments

8.  Commission Initiatives.

9.  Adjournment.

In the event that the Planning Commission meeting of April 6, 2022
is not held, or is concluded prior to a public hearing or other
agenda item being considered, the public hearing or non-public
hearing agenda item will automatically be continued to the next
regular Planning Commission meeting.

Hearing materials are available at:
https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/Planning-Commission-4 and
at City Hall, 1st Floor Lobby Information Desk during regular business
hours. If any additional documents are received for distribution to the
Planning Commission after publication of this Agenda but before 12:00
P.M. on the day of the meeting, they will be made available for public
inspection at the following webpage:
https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/Planning-Commission-4.

(Note: The above procedures are subject to change for future Commission
meetings. Please refer to future Planning Commission agendas for public
participation option procedures at that time.)

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, APRIL 6, 2022

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:
The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, April 6, 2022, in the City Council
Chambers, on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge
of Allegiance by Commissioner David Rice, the meeting was called
to order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:
Present: Chairman Larry Springs
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide Trejo
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams
Excused
Absence: Commissioner Patricia Patrick

Staff:  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., ECDD Director
  Bernard McCrumby, Acting Planning Manager
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Arturo Salazar, Planner
  Angel Leon-Martell, Assistant Planner
  Christine Rivera, Assistant Planner
  Michael Pan, Acting Assistant City Attorney
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary
  Via Community Phone Call Coverage:
  AT&T Conference Call Operator Rep.

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:
Mr. McCrumby, Acting Planning Manager announced that Commissioner
Patricia Patrick, contacted staff that she will not be attending
tonight’s Planning Commission Meeting.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None (Confirmed by AT&T Operator).

(5) MINUTES APPROVAL:
Chairman Springs called for a vote to approve March 2, 2022
minutes.

Motion to Approve March 2, 2022 Minutes by Commissioner Rice and
second by Commissioner Trejo.

The motion passed with the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Commissioners Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and Chairman
  Springs.

(6) NON-PUBLIC HEARINGS:

6A: DESIGN REVIEW NO. 2022-005 (DR-2022-005), 110 NORTH LA BREA
AVENUE.
A non-public hearing to consider new rooftop solar panels on an
existing, 4-story medical office building parking structure on an
H-C (Historic Core) zoned property at 110 North La Brea Avenue.

Mr. Angel Leon-Martell, Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff –
 Can the solar panels be seen?
   Mr. Leon-Martell responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
April 6, 2022
Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
 Will the solar panels cover the entire roof area?
   Mr. Leon-Martell responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward to address
the Planning Commission and speak about their project.

Ms. Jennifer Weskalnies representing the GPM Group, Ameresco, and
Kaiser, along with Mr. Justin Loveall; spoke to the Planning
Commission via telephone regarding the project and to answer
questions from the Planning Commission.

Chairman Springs opened the floor for the Planning Commission to
address the applicant.

Commissioner Rice asked the applicant questions –
 With the elevation of the solar structure, will the glare
  project onto the One Stop Structure across the street?
  - Mr. Leon-Martell, Planning Staff responded to Commissioner
  Rice’s question.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant –
 Do the solar panels move with the sun to absorb the sun?
 Why has this project come into fruition?
  - Ms. Weskalnies responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked the applicant –
 Who will maintain and will there be maintenance on the solar
  panels?
  - Ms. Weskalnies responded to Commissioner Shaw-Williams’
  question.

Chairman Springs closed the non-public hearing and called for a
motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner Shaw-Williams made the motion to affirm the
categorical exemption EA-CE-2022-026 and adopt the attached
resolution approving DR-2022-005, subject to 8 conditions, and
was seconded by Commissioner Trejo, that Resolution No. 1927

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING AN
  APPLICATION  BY  JENIFER  E.  WESKALNIES
  REPRESENTING KAISER FOUNDATION FOR DESIGN
  REVIEW (DR-2022-005) TO APPROVE NEW ROOFTOP
  SOLAR PANELS ON AN EXISTING APPROXIMATELY
  95,000 SQUARE-FOOT 4-STORY PARKING STRUCTURE
  ATTACHED TO AN APPROXIMATELY 61,000 SQUARE-
  FOOT 4-STORY MEDICAL OFFICE BUILDING AN
  APPROXIMATELY  42,000  SQUARE-FOOT  H-C
  (HISTORIC CORE) ZONED PROPERTY LOCATED AT 110
  NORTH LA BREA AVENUE.

Be approved

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Commissioners Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and Chairman
  Springs

Mr. Bernard McCrumby explained the appeal process.

 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
April 6, 2022

6B: DESIGN REVIEW NO. 2022-006 (DR-2022-006), 132 NORTH MARKET
STREET.
A non-public hearing to consider exterior alterations to an
existing two-story commercial building on an H-C (Historic Core)
zoned property at 132 North Market Street.

Mr. Arturo Salazar, Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff –
 For clarification, will the outside patio open up to 4-feet?
 The patio area is 2-feet beyond the overhead awning?
   Mr. Salazar responded to Commissioner Rice’s questions.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
  What was the property area used for before the agreement with
  the applicant?
  Is this project now taking away any of the parking spaces?
  Is there any restitution to the City or is there any recompense
  for the City allowing this project to go forth?
   Mr. Salazar responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to address the Planning
Commission and speak about their project.

Mr. Brion Moran, representing Aero Collective and The Dime; spoke
to the Planning Commission via telephone regarding the project to
answer questions from the Planning Commission.

Chairman Springs opened the floor for the Planning Commission to
address the applicant.

Commissioner Trejo made a statement and asked the applicant –
 Great design and layout and looking forward to this project
  opening.
 The sign design on the building, will it be lit like the
  presentation with Neon?
  - Mr. Moran responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams made a statement and asked the
applicant –
 She too appreciates the new design and
 Do you have a completion date for this project?
  - Mr.  Moran  responded  to  Commissioner  Shaw-Williams’
  question.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant –
 What will happen to the outdoor seating furniture?
 Will there be any food service on site?
  - Mr. Moran responded to Chairman Springs’ question.

Chairman Springs closed the non-public hearing and called for a
motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner Trejo made the motion to affirm categorical
exemption EA-CE-2022-032, and adopt the attached resolution
approving DR-2022-006, subject to the 9 conditions and was
seconded by Commissioner Shaw-Williams, that Resolution No. 1928

  APPROVE EXTERIOR ALTERATIONS TO AN EXISTING

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and Chairman

Mr. Bernard McCrumby explained the appeal process.

(7) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None, (Confirmed by AT&T Operator).

Chairman Springs closed the hearings to the public and asked for
the Planning Commission Initiatives.

(8) COMMISSION INITIATIVES:
Commissioner Trejo -
 Wanted to say thank you to Ms. Mindy Wilcox and Mr. Christopher
  Jackson and to the Planning staff, for orchestrating the
  Planning Commissioners trip to the Conference in San Ramon,
  California.
 First thought that the mall location might have been under-
  utilized by the public, but in the mid-afternoons and on the
  weekends, the saturation of children and all ages was amazing.
 Also, surprised how the other cities in attendance were in awe
  at how Inglewood, a little city that has been able to do so
  much.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams –
 Thank you to the Planning Staff, Ms. Wilcox and Mr. Jackson for
  a great Planning Commission Conference trip to San Ramon and
  also wanted to mention Happy Easter to all.

Chairman Springs -
 Also wanted to join in with his colleagues in thanking both Ms.
  Wilcox and Mr. Jackson for ensuring that they were able to
  attend the Planning Commission Conference in San Ramon.
 Please see if the Planning Commission could have a tour of the
  new housing projects and the businesses being built at the
  Hollywood Park area, prior to completion.
 Wishing everyone a Blessed Happy Easter.
